_about: The judgment hub (plan 7.6f, third round). The words are the card's own and their counterparts: the Greek verb κρίνω, the nouns κρίσις and κρίμα, the judge κριτής, the judgment seat βῆμα, and the compounds of condemning (κατακρίνω, κατάκριμα, κατάκρισις); the Hebrew verb שָׁפַט, the nouns מִשְׁפָּט and שֶׁפֶט, and דִּין, דַּיָּן (also in the Aramaic of Daniel and Ezra). The Greek Old Testament renders מִשְׁפָּט by κρίμα and κρίσις and שָׁפַט by κρίνω, which is why they stand together; each verse still names the word it stands on, and the hub never says they are one word. 'sense' keeps a word only where its verse renders it as judging, judgment or justice: מִשְׁפָּט is also 'ordinance', 'custom' and 'regulation' (about two verses in five), and those are another sense. The frames carry the agent of only some of the Hebrew verb verses and no record of the participle ('the Judge', 'judges'), so the rows on who judges are made by hand where the text names who judges (the divine persons by hand); the nouns are sorted by the words in the verse (in_verse). The contested points -- the final judgment and what follows it, judgment by works beside being counted righteous by faith, and the justice of Israel's courts as its own sense -- are set side by side, the text on each side, each with a note that the page takes no side. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/judgment.json.

titles.noun: What the text says of judgment

_words_why: The card's own (κρίνω, κρίσις, κρίμα, דִּין, δίκη; γνώμη is named apart under the other words) and the family around them: κριτής 'judge' (17 verses), βῆμα 'judgment seat' (10), δικαιοκρισία 'righteous judgment' (Rom 2:5), and the compounds of condemning κατακρίνω (18), κατάκριμα (3) and κατάκρισις (2), which are the verdict itself (Rom 8:1 'no condemnation'; John 8:11); ἀνακρίνω is kept only where the Berean's gloss is 'judge' (1 Cor 2:15, 4:4), its twelve other verses are 'examine'. Hebrew: שָׁפַט (180 verses; the participle is 'the judge', 'the judges'), מִשְׁפָּט (240), שֶׁפֶט 'acts of judgment' (16), the two דִּין (verb 'judge, vindicate' and noun 'cause'), the Aramaic דִּין of Daniel 7 (court, judgment) and the two דַּיָּן 'judge, defender'. The Hebrew words for 'righteousness' are not in the words; the righteousness hub holds them, and the row 'Justice and righteousness' here names the verses where both stand. Left out as different words, and named apart: רָשַׁע (declare guilty), καταδικάζω, καταγινώσκω, κριτικός (Heb 4:12), γνώμη 'opinion' (printed 'judgment' at 1 Cor 7:25).
_sense_why: Measured on MACULA's gloss in each verse. Kept: judge, judgment, justice, condemn, vindicate, defend, decide (a case), plead, court, cause, case, sentence, penalty, rulers (the Hebrew 'judges' are 'rulers' at Amos 2:3, Hos 7:7). Dropped as another sense: מִשְׁפָּט as 'ordinance', 'custom', 'regulation', 'prescribed', 'manner', 'share', 'plan' (163 of 403 verses: Lev 18:4, Deut 4:5, 1 Kgs 8:58, Ps 119's 'ordinances' where the gloss says so, Ezek 20's 'ordinances'); ἀνακρίνω as 'examine' (Acts 17:11); κρίνω as 'decided' (Acts 16:4, 20:16, 25:25, 1 Cor 2:1, Tit 3:12) and 'concluded' (2 Cor 5:14). Held out by hand where the gloss passes but the verse says another thing: Lev 19:35 (measures), Acts 3:13 and 21:25 and 15:19 (a decision), 1 Cor 7:37 and 2 Cor 2:1 (made up my mind). Kept by hand where the gloss says 'right' and the verse means a claim in law: Isa 40:27, Isa 32:7, Job 34:6.

sense_drop.Lev.19.35: מִשְׁפָּט is 'measure' here (dishonest measures of length, weight, volume), not judgment
sense_drop.Acts.3.13: κρίνω is 'decided' (Pilate had decided to release Him), not judging
sense_drop.Acts.21.25: κρίνω is 'decided' (we have written our decision), not judging
sense_drop.Acts.15.19: κρίνω is 'decide' (my judgment is that we should not trouble the Gentiles), a ruling of the council, not judging
sense_drop.1Cor.7.37: κρίνω is 'decided' (has decided in his own heart), not judging
sense_drop.2Cor.2.1: κρίνω is 'decided' (I made up my mind), not judging

sense_keep.Isa.40.27: mishpat 'my right', the cause I am owed
sense_keep.Isa.32.7: mishpat 'the plea of the needy is just'

others._why: Different words the Berean also renders judge, judgment or condemn, named apart with their verses and never handed over as the same word (as love names φιλέω). רָשַׁע is the Hebrew for declaring guilty; καταδικάζω and καταγινώσκω are Greek words for condemning that are not the κρίνω family; γνώμη is 'opinion'.
others.title: Other words translated “judge”, “judgment”, “condemn”

g1106.note: γνώμη means opinion, purpose, resolve. The Berean prints “judgment” at 1 Cor 7:25 (“I give a judgment as one who by the Lord's mercy is trustworthy”) and “conviction” at 1 Cor 1:10. It is not the word for a verdict, and the page does not make the two words one.

h7561.note: רָשַׁע is “be wicked”, and in the form used here, “declare guilty”: “so that the innocent may be acquitted and the guilty condemned” (Deut 25:1). A different word from שָׁפַט, which is the court's judging; the page does not make the two words one.

g2613.note: καταδικάζω is a different Greek word for condemning from κατακρίνω: “you would not have condemned the innocent” (Matt 12:7), “You have condemned and murdered the righteous” (Jas 5:6).

g2607.note: καταγινώσκω, “to find fault with, to condemn”: “Even if our hearts condemn us, God is greater than our hearts, and He knows all things” (1 John 3:20).

g2924.note: κριτικός is “able to discern”: “It judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart” (Heb 4:12).

_review: Not yet reviewed when built. Written against the brief for the third round of hubs (2026-10-25). 26 rows (15 noun, 11 verb), over the brief's 15-25, because the noun and the verb are different records in the data (the frames carry the verb, the phrases the noun) and the rows on who judges (God; Jesus; 'the Lord, He, the One'; those told to judge; those told not to; the judges of Israel) are by hand. Reviewed by the eleven-seat panel the same day; the fixes, held items and declined items are in _review_2026_10_25.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Verb row 'Judging the living and the dead, the world, the nations' relabelled 'Judging the earth, the peoples and the nations; judging the living and the dead', so the phrase from 2 Tim 4:1 and 1 Pet 4:5-6 is not laid over Isa 2:4, Ps 96:13 and Joel 3:12.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Ps 96:13 says 'He is coming to judge the earth' and Isa 2:4 'He will judge between the nations'; the label now says what each verse says.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Jas 5:9 removed from 'Told not to judge, and rebuked for judging'; it stays in noun row 'A judge, the Judge' and is named under the verb 'Every other use'.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Berean: 'Do not complain about one another, brothers, so that you will not be judged. Look, the Judge is standing at the door!': it rebukes grumbling, not judging.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Noun row on the world and the nations: 1 John 4:17 removed; relabelled 'Judgment on the nations and the world; justice for the nations'; examples now lead with Isa 42:1 instead of Matt 12:18; note added that Isa 42 and 51 speak of justice going out to the nations and that who the Servant of Isa 42:1 is readers take differently.
_review_2026_10_25.why: 1 John 4:17 is the day of judgment (already in that row) and is on this one only because 'world' is in the English; the Old Testament verse leads, and the note takes no side.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Merge the verb rows 'Judged, and works, deeds, ways' and 'Judged, and believing, faith' into one so no order remains to read.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The scholar's reasoning argues against it (it would merge the very pair the page declines to settle); for the editor: the order of two rows on a contested pair, or one row of 21. Ruled: the two verb rows stay separate, 'Judged, and believing, faith' first and 'Judged, and works, deeds, ways' second, both notes saying the rows are in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking; the noun pair is left as it is. Doug, 2026-10-25, rulings sheet: as recommended.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Move Ps 1:5 from the day-of-judgment row to 'In the gate and the court'.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Whether Ps 1:5 'will not stand in the judgment' is a court or the last day is itself a point readers take differently, and the teacher's reasoning is that the day row has almost no Old Testament left; the editor decides. Ruled: Ps 1:5 stays in the day-of-judgment row and also stands in 'In the gate and the court', with a note under the day row that it is read of a court and of the last day and the page does not choose. Doug, 2026-10-25, rulings sheet: as recommended.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Noun 'Every other use' note now says that about 163 verses where mishpat means statute, ordinance or custom (for example Deut 4:5 and Lev 18:4) are another sense of the word and are not shown.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Measured in the build (163 of 403 verses); the page no longer presents the word as judgment throughout.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Noun rows reordered so the Hebrew-led ones come first (justice for the poor; justice and righteousness; the gate and the court; the king; the LORD's justice; justice asked of God; justice turned away among people; judgments on the peoples; a judge; then the nations, the day, works, condemnation, mercy, what follows, particular acts, every other use). own_words now opens with Gen 18:25, Amos 5:24 and Ps 96:13.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Hebrew mishpat is 240 uses and the later sense is drawn from it; the order is the Old Testament first and settles no doctrine. The relative order of works and condemnation is as it was; membership does not change (match all).

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Deut 32:4, Jer 22:13 and Jer 7:5 taken out of 'Judgment and works, deeds'.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Deut 32:4 is God's work and stands in the LORD's justice row; Jer 22:13 is a woe on a king who builds without justice; Jer 7:5 is a call to act justly: none is a judging of deeds. The deeds that ground a judgment (John 5:29, 2 Cor 5:10, Eccl 12:14, Rom 2:5, Jude 15) stay.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Jude 4 taken out of the mercy row and put in the new row of judgment on particular acts; that row relabelled 'Justice with loving devotion, mercy, grace: “The LORD loves righteousness and justice”; “mercy triumphs over judgment”' and led by Ps 33:5, Hos 2:19, Mic 6:8, Jas 2:13.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Jude 4 is grace misused and condemnation of those who misuse it, not a pairing; the Hebrew pairs are most of the row. Jude 4 went to the particular-acts row, not the condemnation row, because that row is the words κατάκριμα and κατάκρισις and Jude 4 has κρίμα.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: 'What follows' note rewritten: “the fire of hell” (Matt 5:22) and “the sentence of hell” (Matt 23:33), the Greek being geenna in both; the quotation marks round 'fires of Gehenna' dropped.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Berean Matt 23:33: 'How will you escape the sentence of hell?'; there is no fire in that verse.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: 'What follows' note now says the row holds only verses that use a word for judgment and that the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46), gathered with this card, is not in it.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The limit was stated only in the builder's report; a reader of a nine-verse row could take it for all the text on the question.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: 'Justice and righteousness' relabelled as the Hebrew pair mishpat and tsedaqah, with a note naming the Greek verses (John 16:8, Acts 24:25, 2 Cor 3:9, 2 Tim 4:8) as other words; the lead no longer opens on a Greek verse.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The Greek members stand beside krisis, krima, katakrisis and kritēs, not the word for justice; the note says so and the page does not make them one word.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: A separate short row 'Judgment, condemnation and righteousness (Greek)' for those four verses.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The reviewer offered the note as the alternative; a new row of four takes the hub further from 15-25 and the note carries the distinction.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: 'Justice denied, perverted, asked for' split in two: justice asked of God (Job, Isa 40:27, 49:4, Jer 12:1, Mal 2:17, Hab 1:4, Ps 17:2) and justice turned away among people (Isa 59:8-15, Eccl 3:16 and 5:8, Lam 3:35, Hab 1:4).
_review_2026_10_25.why: Isa 59:9 'justice is far from us' is the people's own confession and Eccl 3:16 'in the place of judgment there is wickedness' is an observation; neither is a charge against God. Lam 3:35 ('to deny a man justice before the Most High') is put with the people, not with the complaint to God as the reviewer listed it, because the verse is about what people do.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Amos 5:12 added to the justice-among-people row.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The verse has no word of the judgment family: the Berean's 'deprive the poor of justice' renders a verb meaning 'push aside'.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Note on the noun king row: whom the verses of Isa 9:7, 16:5, 32:1 and Jer 23:5 mean readers take differently; the page does not choose.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The verb row already carries the same note for Isa 11:3-4; the same kind of verse is now handled the same way.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: A row 'Judgment falling on particular acts' for the verses that were in the noun catch-all (Matt 5:21, Rom 3:8, Rom 13:2, Mark 12:40, 1 Cor 11:29 and 11:34, Jas 3:1, Jas 5:12, Gal 5:10, 1 Tim 3:6, 5:12 and 5:24, 2 Pet 2:4) with Jude 4; the catch-all keeps the breastpiece, the Urim, the lot and Jude 9.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Each of these is judgment or condemnation falling on a person or an act; filing them as 'other' cut them from the verses they belong with.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Verb row 'Judged by “the Lord”, “He”, “the One”' relabelled 'Judging by one the verse calls “the Lord”, “He”, “the One” or describes: “the Man He has appointed”, “Faithful and True”'.
_review_2026_10_25.why: In Rev 6:10 the verse names its addressee and in Acts 17:31 it describes him; the label now says so. A relabel to the verse's own words only; no verse moved.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Fold 'Justice for the poor' into 'Justice and righteousness' to cut a row.
_review_2026_10_25.why: The Torah's justice for the poor, the fatherless, the widow and the foreigner is the heart of the courts' own sense and would be buried in a row of 71; the 28 rows are accepted because the noun and the verb are separate records.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: A door from the condemnation row to the righteousness card, so the verdict 'justify' (Rom 5:16-18; 8:33-34) stays beside 'condemn'.
_review_2026_10_25.why: A door only; no verse added and no side taken.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: By-hand rows or notes for texts with no judgment word: the Hebrew day-of-the-LORD texts (Joel 1:15, Amos 5:18, Zeph 1:14, Isa 13:9), the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46), 1 Cor 3:15, Rom 4:5, and the annihilationist and universalist proof-texts.
_review_2026_10_25.why: Scope: whether the hub holds only verses with a judgment word is the editor's decision; Matt 25 names the Son of Man, a divine person by hand; and the rows would put one side's proof-texts on a contested point. The page now says the limit. Ruled: no new rows; the day-of-judgment row gets a door to the wrath card and a note that the Hebrew 'Day of the LORD' texts use other words and are not on this page (Isa 13:13 and Zeph 1:15 are on the wrath page, Amos 5:18 on the light page, and the sheep and the goats is gathered with this page). Doug, 2026-10-25, rulings sheet: as recommended.

_review_2026_10_25.fix: Add Rom 2:5 to the day-of-judgment row ('the day of wrath').
_review_2026_10_25.why: The reviewer offered it as 'could'; the verse stands in the works and the LORD's justice rows already, and the placement is the editor's. Ruled: Rom 2:5 also stands in the day-of-judgment row. Doug, 2026-10-25, rulings sheet: as recommended.

rows.label: Justice for the poor, the fatherless, the widow, the foreigner
Justice and righteousness (the Hebrew pair mishpat and tsedaqah)
rows.note: Most of these verses are Hebrew, where the Berean prints “justice” for mishpat and “righteousness” for tsedaqah or tsedeq. A few are Greek (John 16:8, Acts 24:25, 2 Cor 3:9, 2 Tim 4:8): there “righteousness” stands beside the Greek words for judgment (krisis, krima), condemnation (katakrisis) or the judge (kritēs), which are other words, and the page does not make them one with the Hebrew.

rows.label: In the gate and the court: judges, elders, witnesses, bribes; trials and sentences

not_verses.Job.32.9: 'it is not only the old who understand justice': the elders are wise, not judges in a court

rows._why: God's justice in the law courts of Israel as its own sense (the brief): the gate where the elders sat, the judges Moses appointed, the case brought to the judge (Deut 17:8-11), the witness and the bribe. The same row holds the courts of Rome the New Testament names (Pilate's, Gallio's, Festus's judgment seat) and the sentences kings pass, since the Berean prints them with the same word.

rows.label: The king and the throne: “the king for judgment”, kings who do justice, the throne

not_verses.Ezek.7.27: 'the king will mourn': the judgments are on the whole people
not_verses.2Kgs.25.6: the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah: in 'In the gate and the court'
not_verses.Jer.39.5: the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah: in 'In the gate and the court'
not_verses.Jer.52.9: the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah: in 'In the gate and the court'

rows.note: In Isa 9:7, 16:5, 32:1 and Jer 23:5 the king the prophet describes is one whom readers take differently; the page does not choose.

rows.label: The LORD's justice and judgments: “a God of justice”, “true and just are Your judgments”
rows._why: by hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names the LORD or God, or is addressed to Him ('Righteous are You, O LORD', Ps 119:137; 'uphold their cause', 1 Kgs 8:45)

rows.label: Justice asked of God, and the answer: “God has deprived me of justice”, “Does God pervert justice?”, “Where is the God of justice?”
rows.note: The complaint and the answer stand together as the text has them: Job says God has taken away his justice (27:2), Elihu that God does not pervert it (34:12), and those Malachi speaks to ask “Where is the God of justice?” (2:17). The page does not choose between them.
rows._why: hard verses stay (rule 7 of the brief): the Bible asks whether God is just, and the question belongs to the word. Split from the verses where people turn justice away (the next row) after the review: Isa 59 and Eccl 3:16 are not a charge against God. Hab 1:4 stands in both.

rows.label: Justice turned away and perverted among people: “justice is turned away”, “in the place of judgment there is wickedness”, “the denial of justice and righteousness in the province”
rows.note: Here the verses speak of people turning justice away: the people's own words in Isa 59 (“justice is far from us”, 59:9), what Ecclesiastes saw in the place of judgment (3:16; 5:8), “to deny a man justice before the Most High” (Lam 3:35), and the wicked who hem in the righteous (Hab 1:4). They are set apart from the row before, where justice is asked of God.

rows.label: Judgments on Egypt, Moab, Edom, Babylon, Sidon, Thebes; judgments on Judah, Israel and Jerusalem

not_verses.1Kgs.11.33: Chemosh, Moab's god, is named for the idolatry; the 'judgments' are the LORD's ordinances Solomon did not keep
not_verses.2Kgs.25.6: the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah: a sentence of a court, in 'In the gate and the court'
not_verses.Jer.39.5: the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah: in 'In the gate and the court'
not_verses.Jer.52.9: the king of Babylon passes sentence on Zedekiah: in 'In the gate and the court'

rows._why: by the names of the peoples in the verse, and by hand the judgments on His own people (Ezekiel's 'judgments', Hosea's lawsuit, Mal 3:5 'I will draw near to you for judgment'), each only where the verse has the noun

rows.label: A judge, the Judge; “all judgment to the Son”
rows.note: The text names the judge in several ways: “God, the Judge of all” (Heb 12:23), “the One appointed by God as Judge of the living and the dead” (Acts 10:42), “the righteous Judge” whom Paul calls “the Lord” (2 Tim 4:8), “one Lawgiver and Judge” (Jas 4:12), “the Judge is standing at the door” (Jas 5:9), and also earthly judges and the judge in Jesus' parable of the widow (Luke 18:2). In John 5:22 the Father “has entrusted all judgment to the Son”; in John 9:39 Jesus says “For judgment I have come into this world”. Where the verse says only “the Lord” or “the Judge”, readers take it of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: κριτής and דַּיָּן in the verse, and by hand (divine persons by hand) the verses where Jesus or the Son is named with judgment (John 5:22, 5:27, 5:30, 8:16, 9:39)

rows.label: Judgment on the nations and the world; justice for the nations

not_verses.Acts.24.10: Paul says Felix has been 'a judge over this nation' for many years: a judge of men, in 'A judge, the Judge'
not_verses.1John.4.17: 'confidence on the day of judgment': the day, in the row for the day of judgment; 'world' is only in the English of the verse

rows.note: Isa 42 and 51 speak of justice going out to the nations; Matt 12:18-20 quotes Isa 42:1-4. Who the Servant of Isa 42:1 is, readers take differently; the page does not choose.

rows.label: The day of judgment, the hour of judgment; “at the judgment”; “after that to face judgment”; the judgment seat of God; the court seated, the books opened

not_verses.2Tim.4.8: the word is κριτής, 'the righteous Judge', and 'that day' is the crown's day; it stands in 'A judge, the Judge'
not_verses.2Pet.2.4: the verse has no word for 'day': the angels are 'held for judgment'; it stands in 'Judgment falling on particular acts'

rows.note: Ps 1:5 (“the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous”) is read of a court and of the last day, and the page does not choose; it also stands in “In the gate and the court”. The Hebrew “Day of the LORD” texts (Joel 1:15, Amos 5:18, Zeph 1:14, Isa 13:9) use other words and are not on this page; Isa 13:13 and Zeph 1:15 are on the wrath page, Amos 5:18 is on the light page, and the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46) is gathered with this page.
rows._why: The text's own phrases. Rom 14:10 and 2 Cor 5:10 are the two verses that call the judgment seat God's and Christ's; the other four uses of βῆμα (Pilate, Gallio, Festus) are earthly courts, in 'In the gate and the court'.

rows.label: Judgment and works, deeds

not_verses.Exod.28.15: the 'work' is the skilled craftsman's, the breastpiece of judgment
not_verses.Ps.111.7: 'the works of His hands are faithful and just' is God's work, not a judgment by deeds
not_verses.Deut.32.4: 'His work is perfect; all His ways are just': God's work, not a judging of deeds; it stands in 'The LORD's justice and judgments'
not_verses.Jer.22.13: a woe on the king who builds 'without justice' and pays no wages: not a judging of deeds
not_verses.Jer.7.5: a call to 'correct your ways and deeds' and 'act justly': a call to act, not a judging of deeds

rows.note: Set side by side with the rows on condemnation and on believing, as the text has them; a verse that names more than one stands in each. Where Christian traditions part on how judgment by works stands to being counted righteous by faith, the page takes no side.
rows._why: ἔργον, πρᾶξις, πράσσω, מַעֲשֶׂה, מַעֲלָל in the verse. 'Ways' (דֶּרֶךְ, ὁδός) were in the rule at first and took 'all His ways are just' (Deut 32:4), 'the way of the wicked' (Jer 12:1) and 'on the way to court' (Matt 5:25): they are out. Rom 2:5 ('righteous judgment') names no deed but 2:6 does; Ezek 7:27 says 'according to their way I will deal with them'. Deut 32:4, Jer 22:13 and Jer 7:5 were taken out after the review (2026-10-25).

rows.label: Condemnation, and “no condemnation”; “does not come into judgment”
rows.note: The Greek κατάκριμα and κατάκρισις, “condemnation”. Rom 5:16-18 sets the judgment that followed one trespass “to condemnation” beside the gift that follows many; Rom 8:1 says there is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus; John 5:24 says the one who hears and believes “does not come into judgment”. Set beside the row on works, as the text has them. Where Christian traditions part on how these stand to one another, and on how far “all” reaches in Rom 5:18, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Justice with loving devotion, mercy, grace: “The LORD loves righteousness and justice”; “mercy triumphs over judgment”

not_verses.Jude.1.4: grace misused and the condemnation of those who misuse it, not a pairing of judgment and grace; it stands in 'Judgment falling on particular acts'

rows.note: The text's own pairs. The page does not say how they are reconciled.

rows.label: Judgment and what follows, in the text's own words: eternal, fire, destruction, Gehenna

not_verses.John.5.24: 'eternal life' is the gift of the one who does not come into judgment; it stands in 'Condemnation, and no condemnation'

rows.note: The words the verses use: “eternal judgment” (Heb 6:2), “eternal destruction” (2 Thess 1:9), “eternal fire” (Jude 7), “destruction of the ungodly” (2 Pet 3:7), “the fire of hell” (Matt 5:22) and “the sentence of hell” (Matt 23:33), where the Greek is geenna in both. Where Christian traditions part on what follows the final judgment -- punishment without end, an end of the wicked, or the restoration of all -- the page takes no side; it sets the verses as they stand. This row holds only verses that use a word for judgment: the sheep and the goats (Matt 25:31-46), gathered with this card, is not in it.

rows.label: Judgment falling on particular acts: murder, resisting authority, eating and drinking without recognizing the body, would-be teachers, oaths, defrauding widows, turning grace into license
rows.note: Among them: murder (Matt 5:21), resisting authority (Rom 13:2), eating and drinking without recognizing the body (1 Cor 11:29), would-be teachers (Jas 3:1), oaths (Jas 5:12: “fall under judgment”), defrauding widows of their houses (Mark 12:40: “greater condemnation”), ungodly men who turn the grace of God into a license for immorality (Jude 4), the angels who sinned, “held for judgment” (2 Pet 2:4), and Rom 3:8, “their condemnation is deserved”.
rows._why: by hand: these were in the noun catch-all, and each is judgment or condemnation falling on a person or an act. Moved here after the review (2026-10-25); the catch-all keeps the breastpiece, the Urim, the lot and Jude 9.

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Among them: the breastpiece of judgment and the Urim (Exod 28:15-30; Num 27:21) and the lot (Prov 16:33); Jude 9, where the Greek is “a judgment of blasphemy” and the Berean prints “slanderous charge”. About 163 verses where the Hebrew mishpat means statute, ordinance or custom (for example Deut 4:5 and Lev 18:4) are another sense of the word and are not shown on this page.

rows.label: God judges, and is asked to judge: “the Judge of all the earth”, “May the LORD judge between us”, “vindicate me”
rows._why: by hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names the LORD, God or 'the Judge' as the one who judges, or asks Him to. Job 9:15 and 23:7 'my Judge' and Isa 33:22 'the LORD is our Judge' are the Hebrew participle, which the frames do not carry. Isa 43:26 ('let us argue our case together') is left under 'Every other use': the LORD and Israel are both parties.

rows.label: Jesus: “I judge”, “I do not judge”, “has entrusted all judgment to the Son”, “who will judge the living and the dead”
rows.note: By hand: the verses where the text itself names Jesus, Christ or the Son, or has Jesus say “I”. They sit side by side as they stand -- “I judge no one” (John 8:15), “I do not judge him” (John 12:47), “I judge as I hear” (John 5:30), “the word I spoke will judge him on the last day” (John 12:48) -- and the page does not reconcile them.

rows.label: Judging by one the verse calls “the Lord”, “He”, “the One” or describes: “the Man He has appointed”, “Faithful and True”
rows.note: The text says “the Lord”, “He”, “the One”, or describes him -- “Faithful and True” (Rev 19:11), “the Man He has appointed” (Acts 17:31), “Him who is ready to judge” (1 Pet 4:5), “One who seeks it and judges” (John 8:50). Readers take these of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.

rows.label: Told to judge, and promised judging: “judge righteously”, “judge for yourselves”, “the saints will judge the world”, “twelve thrones”
rows.note: Set beside the row that follows, as the text has them; the page does not say how they are reconciled.

rows.label: Told not to judge, and rebuked for judging: “Do not judge, or you will be judged”, “who are you to judge your neighbor?”, “stop judging by outward appearances”
The judges: Moses, the judges of Israel, Samuel, the king, elders and priests judge the people; “who made you ruler and judge over us?”, “judged Israel twenty-three years”
rows.note: In Isa 11:3-4 the one who “will judge the poor with righteousness” is the shoot from the stump of Jesse (11:1); whom the verse means readers take differently, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: by hand: the Hebrew participle (the judges) is not in the frames, so the forty verses of 'pick' are those the word-by-word text shows; 'add' keeps the verses the frames carry, each only where the verse has the word

rows.label: Judged, and believing, faith: “whoever believes in Him is not condemned”, “by faith Noah ... condemned the world”

not_verses.Acts.17.31: πίστις here is 'proof' (God has given proof to all by raising Him), not faith

rows.note: These two rows are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking. Mark 16:16 stands in the longer ending (16:9-20) that the earliest manuscripts lack. Where Christian traditions part on how faith and works stand to the judgment, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Judged, and works, deeds, ways: “according to each one's work”, “according to his deeds”, “according to your ways”

not_verses.1Sam.8.5: 'you walk not in your ways': the elders ask for a king 'to judge us'; the ways are Samuel's sons', not the ground of a judgment

rows.note: These two rows are listed in the alphabetical order of their labels and carry no ranking. Where Christian traditions part on how judgment by works stands to being counted righteous by faith, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Judging the earth, the peoples and the nations; judging the living and the dead
rows.note: Where Christian traditions part on the final judgment and what follows it -- punishment without end, an end of the wicked, or the restoration of all -- the page takes no side; the verses are set as they stand. Rev 20:12-13 and 1 Pet 4:6 are among the hardest, and are here.

rows.label: Condemn, condemned: “neither do I condemn you”, “who is the one who condemns?”, “will condemn this generation”
rows.note: The Greek verb κατακρίνω. It is said of the men who condemn Jesus to death (Matt 20:18; Mark 10:33; 14:64), of God who “condemned sin in the flesh” (Rom 8:3) and the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah (2 Pet 2:6), and of Jesus who says “neither do I condemn you” (John 8:11). Mark 16:16 stands in the longer ending (16:9-20) that the earliest manuscripts lack.
rows._why: by hand, because the frames lack John 8:10 and Rom 8:34; these are the eighteen verses of κατακρίνω

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Among them: Gen 19:9, the men of Sodom (“he is already acting like a judge!”); Matt 5:40 and 1 Cor 6:1-6, going to law; Luke 19:22, “I will judge you by your own words”; Rom 2:12, 2:27 and Jas 2:12, judged by the law; Jas 5:9, “so that you will not be judged”, said to those who grumble against one another; Ps 82:2, God's question to the judges (“How long will you judge unjustly?”); Isa 43:26, the LORD and Israel arguing their case; Job 22:13, the question Eliphaz puts to Job (“Does He judge through thick darkness?”); Acts 23-26, Paul on trial.
